 Craig Weighs In On Blue Line’s Lack Of Offensive Production 
 By Ken Boehlke 
 On November 11, 2026 
 In Game Analysis 
 (Photo Credit: SinBin.vegas Photographer Brandon Andreasen)
 On the recent road trip, the Golden Knights managed to grind their way to seven out of eight points, an unequivocal success. However, the offensive side of the game has still been a bit underwhelming. They scored just 11 goals in four games, with only seven coming at even strength.
 One issue we’ve highlighted on SinBin.vegas is the lack of offense from the blue line. Vegas’ defensemen still account for a league-low share of the team’s points, and their 29 combined points through 19 games now rank 30th in the NHL.
 It hasn’t impacted overall team success as the Golden Knights remain in 2nd place in the division with a solid .684 points percentage, but it may be an early warning of a larger problem.
 We haven’t hung on to pucks maybe as long in the o-zone. That last trip we did a better job of it, but kind of that o-zone time play that leads to power plays or leads to opportunities where you get teams extended, where you get that five-man offensive game. I think we saw signs of that coming back, closer to the start of the year, on the last road trip, that will help our D get involved offensively. -Ryan Craig
 Craig insists, though, that they cannot chase offense at the expense of solid defending. 
 Well, we’re always going to be a check and defend team first. That’s what we are. When we do that, we create our offense out of that. So, I think I talked about our execution kind of two weeks ago now was a little bit off, right? I think it’s probably led a little bit to our breakouts weren’t as clean. That’s an opportunity for our D to activate out of that.
 Whether it’s in-zone or on the rush, there’s no doubt VGK’s blue line has to be more involved in the offense if the team is going to operate at full capacity.
 No Vegas defenseman has scored a goal in the last nine games, and it’s coincided with a massive drop in offensive production from the team overall. In those nine games, the Golden Knights have scored just 22 goals, or 2.44 per game. In the first 10 games, the defensemen scored six, and the offense averaged 4.20 goals per game.
 Tonight is a good opportunity to begin turning it around. The Mammoth have allowed more than 40 goals in their last 10 games, boasting the league’s 2nd worst save percentage (.846) over that span. It’s the perfect chance for Vegas’ blue liners to step up and make an impact in the always difficult first game back from a road trip.
 VGK’s defense corps is far too talented to be held down for much longer. The tide has to turn eventually, and there’s no better time than now.
